summary: Glacier National Park's northernmost lookout, built 1934 on the site of a 1922 fire camp; Edward Abbey staffed it in 1975.

facts.design: two-story, 14x14 ft timber cab with hip roof, standard NPS/USFS plan

staffing.note: the Forest Fire Lookout Association roster only records structure status (standing/gone/ruins), not staffing; no checked source confirms current staffing at Numa Ridge

access.note: reached by public trail from Lake Bowman; lookout cab is an active NPS post, not open for entry or rental

visit.trail_note: trail access from Lake Bowman, Glacier National Park

events.note: site established as a fire camp, then called Indian Ridge
frame cabin added at the 7,100-foot level
current two-story timber lookout built to standard NPS/USFS plan (NRHP nomination text gives 1933)
Edward Abbey staffed the lookout for a summer season
listed on NRHP under Glacier National Park Multiple Resource Area, #86000357
registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, September 15, 1991

evidence.quote: Originally named Indian Ridge and established as a camp in 1922, a frame cabin at the 7100' level was added in 1923.
Numa Ridge Lookout is another of the more common 14'x14' designs with an extended hip roof. Constructed in 1934
The low two-story timber-construction structure with a pyramidal roof was built in 1933.
Author Edward Abbey spent the summer of 1975 manning Numa Ridge Lookout.

evidence.supports: northernmost in park, trail from Lake Bowman
evidence.quote: it is the most northern lookout in the Park, being only nine miles south of the Canadian border. It is reached by trail from Lake Bowman.
Numa Ridge Flathead 48.88366 -114.17959 2-Story cab Standing NHLR US 38, MT 6

evidence.supports: standard plan, chain of overlapping lookouts
evidence.quote: The Numa Ridge Fire Lookout in Glacier National Park is significant as one of a chain of staffed fire lookout posts within the park... The lookout was built to a standard plan originated by the U.S. Forest Service as part of a program to provide overlapping fire lookout coverage within the park.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and firelookout.com both give 1934; the Wikipedia article's NRHP-derived text says 1933. Treated as an unresolved discrepancy in the record rather than picking one.

notes_for_editor: Built-year discrepancy (1933 vs 1934) left unresolved per sources; worth a look at the NPGallery NRHP PDF (86000357) if a firmer date is wanted.
